_doc: Curated classical-Chinese pinyin overrides. pypinyin is tuned for modern Mandarin and systematically mis-reads high-frequency classical polyphones — most notably 为 (defaults to wèi 'for', but the verb reading wéi 'to do/govern/be' dominates in wenyan) and 子 in 子曰 (defaults to neutral zi, should be zǐ 'the Master'). This file supplies verified phrase-level readings consulted by tools/build_pinyin.py via longest-match prefix before falling back to pypinyin. SEED SCOPE: high-frequency, high-confidence cases in Lunyu + Mengzi where pypinyin provably fails. NOT exhaustive — extend as you verify more against zhuyin editions / Legge glosses. Every entry should be defensible from a published reference; when in doubt, leave it out and let the per-char fallback render.
_format: key = phrase (CJK, SIMPLIFIED form — the canon is simplified), value = list of pinyin syllables (one per char, with tone marks). Match is case- and form-sensitive on the exact CJK string. Longest match wins at each position. Re-keyed from traditional to simplified via OpenCC t2s (matching tools/to_simplified.py's repo-wide migration); the original traditional keys silently never matched the simplified chapter text.
_references: James Legge, The Chinese Classics (1861-1872) — pinyin conversion of his glosses
